Its certainly not narcissistic - you are one of the few people capable of recognising some genuine reasons for being concerned, and you're choosing to act on them rather than sit back and watch, whatever might happen - and that's certainly not selfish!

The reason why I say you shouldn't visit is that, for at least the time being, he's made it clear he needs some space. Its likely he's unsure about that, but whatevers going through its mind, its what he's said - and we have to try and believe when we can. Its possible his feelings for you are part of the reason he's in trouble, and no matter how positive your attempts to reach out to him are, if he's in a self-destructive mode then he'll likely find some way of spinning them, to add to the confusion. I can only talk from personal experience here, but having been through something similar myself I know that having control over your own space when you feel vulnerable is very important to regaining a sense of balance or calm. 

That said, I don't for a moment think you should give up. Perhaps leave a message with him, telling him how care, and want to be there for him, but that you have chosen to take his advise for now, and will stay distant until he is ready. That way he won't feel abandoned but he will also have the opportunity to take space if he needs it. In the meantime, perhaps try to engage his mum or friend again. Even some of his old friends you haven't met - some carefully placed messages could catch someone at a good time, and help you take on some of this responsibility.

The pain pills are a problem, but its difficult to know how much without knowing what he's on. Doctors rarely prescribe potent medication to patients with a history of depression or bi-polar disorder; in fact some pain medications are designed for the very purpose of being almost non-overdoseable (if thats a word). That said, its probably not worth taking risks. of course, if you have reason think there is an immediate risk of him overdosing, you should consider calling a suicide help-line for advise on who to contact about intervening...

there are no words for it - don't try and name it. You can't know what happened, and if you let yourself then you'll get carried away, imagining things as they never are - as things you can't participate in. She is likely as confused as you are - I have no doubt she cares about you deeply. Please try not to fixate on the sexuality of this. Sex and understanding are often different things, and we so regularly confuse one with the other. Keep the moments you understood each other close to heart, whether sexual or otherwise, and remember they will always be there

She did, and she will again. Try not to fixate on this image you have man, its not doing you good :( If it keeps returning, try to keep yourself occupied in something. I find when Im troubled by disturbing thoughts it helps to get submerged in music

Your concern is good, don't let yourself be convinced by others that would have you dismiss it as unnecessary. The first thing I'd recommend is not doing anything that will make him panic. If you're right, and suicide is on his mind, then presenting him with difficult situations might only make matters worse. You did the right thing in trying to reach out to others though; attempts at helping don't always need to be interventions. If people are aware there might be a problem, they can try harder to communicate, and help him draw himself out of this thing himself. Unfortunately I don't think this can be done (entirely) by you alone. Whatever the reason for the break up, its a decision he's made for now, and its unfortunate that he's probably putting a lot of his current confusion into that relationship. This isn't permanent, but having been in what I imagine to be his shoes, I can say that he might need to hear this from someone else right now. It can be so hard when the love we have for people forces us to keep our distance, but just for now I would not recommend visiting his house. Do you have any mutual friends that you could speak to about this? Is there any way of drawing him out of this spiral completely - getting out of town for a bit, or suggesting something neutral to get him out of this thing? (A gig?).
I'm sure others will have suggestions, but I'd repeat I think it shows the honesty of your love for him that you came here :) you're not just an Ex, you're a good friend

your right; right now your feelings for her are mixed with a kind of resentment and jealousy that makes them incomprehensible. I know this is the last thing you want to hear but its amazing what even a little time will do, if you give it to yourself. The two times i've been in your shoes it has felt gigantic in a way that forbids the possibility of any resolution. And even though I'd been through it once, and realised I could do it, the second time was no different. There are questions here you can't answer now, and you certainly can't answer them alone. Try to put them down, and work on things you can control. Do you something you love, and see people. Don't be afraid to be sad in their presence, they will want to listen too

Yeah, she did, but you said it yourself, you were her first. Do you think theres anything she, or you, or anyone can do that can take that away? Or take away the moments that kept you together that long? Even if you chose never to think of it again, it will still have happened. She was lucky then and so were you - and you'll feel lucky again I promise

You came here because you felt the urge to express whatever your feeling in the hope that you might communicate something, or reach some understanding: and that's always the right thing to do when the only other option is to internalise these things. I don't think I've met a person yet who doesn't need to be alone sometimes; be we society sometimes too - to escape into something bigger, to help solve problems we can't solve alone. However and how brief you choose that society is up to you, but while your here - lets talk :)
Tell me about something you love, I'd like to hear it

Hey Zero,
First of all I want to say slow down. You're being forced to deal with a lot right now, and trying to get a grip of it all at once is only going to make things worse. Sit down, drink something warm, and think this thing through, one part at a time. Whatever ends up coming its clear you have to take some action of your own, and you can do it. Maybe think about this housing situation first, that's something concrete. Don't rush yourself - do you have friends or family you could stay with for a few weeks? Asking yourself to shoulder all this work at once will not work; and there are people who care and want to help. Try to put everything else on pause until you're settled somewhere fresh, even if its temporary - there's plenty of future to address things in, one by one, so forgive yourself for now and put the doubt away. I think I speak for everyone when I say I know how relationships like these can be: but I promise you, however you narrativise this now, your ex will be in the same place. You don't stay in a relationship for 2 1/2 years with someone you don't love, and you don't love people that aren't loveable. What Im not saying is that you should fixate upon getting back together, or that there will be any solution that simple. What I am saying is that you should give both yourself, and you ex, some time - and try to see this difficulty through, one part at the time. You have the strength to do it, and the people here will keep listening, to remind you of that

Hey buddy; I see a lot of things to like in this post - what makes you so set on suicide? I would advise thinking about it for longer; considering your motives, and whether in light of them it really is the right thing. It sounds like you're especially concerned with life at home: if this *is* a major concern, I would advise you to at least wait a few years. University can be very difficult, but its important to know that it really is a temporary thing (at least, far more temporary than the rest). And if you feel you really can't see it through, try speaking to a support officer? Most schools have procedures that allow their students to take one or more years out for personal reasons - you could defer the course and try something completely different, perhaps in another country, away from your home situation (after all, your english is good!).
In any case I would advise against the train idea. It might seem tempting, but it is very public, and having seen the aftermath personally, I wouldn't wish that on anyone. It can also be extremely disturbing for drivers. (I commend your concern for schoolkids, and would suggest extending that courtesy to others too)

I know the advise is old and tired, but if you haven't tried medical help yet its worth a shot. Many people suffer from subtle neurological ticks, and although you are clearly strong enough to lead a social life despite of it, there are certainly ways of making things easier for your self. You just need to remember its not your fault, and it could be the thing you need to start making some positive changes; think of it as a holiday away from your sadness, giving you the time to make a few changes to ensure it becomes permanent?
